To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

drought tolerance is a complex trait that is associated with a combination of traits that are different from those expected based on evolutionary and ecological processes, and that species-specific differences in drought tolerance are not associated with the same set of traits in all species.

drought tolerance is associated with a specific combination of trait values that are also associated with drought tolerance at the species level; and, although evolutionary and ecological selective processes tend to result in similar trait values, they do not result in identical trait combinations.
drought tolerance is associated with specific combinations of ecophysiological traits and that the combination of traits associated with drought tolerance varies between species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional responses of seedlings of 11 Mediterranean woody species to water stress.
the relationship between individual responses and interspecific trends in the drought tolerance of tree seedlings.
the ecophysiology of Mediterranean tree seedlings, and with the individual and interspecific response to drought.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the functional traits associated with species drought tolerance and with drought responses of individuals are different.
drought tolerance is achieved by different trait values in different species, and that drought induces a shift in trait values within a species.
drought tolerance is a complex trait and that it is difficult to generalize about the functional traits associated with it.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

drought tolerance in the species studied is associated with a combination of traits that include a high photosynthetic capacity, low leaf water potential, low water use efficiency, low leaf area, low specific leaf weight, high leaf mass per area, high leaf area ratio, and high shoot-root ratio.
drought tolerance in Mediterranean tree seedling species is associated with low leaf area, high shoot-root ratio and high leaf area ratio.
drought tolerance is a complex trait, which is achieved through different combinations of functional traits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
drought-tolerant plants are not a single functional group and, therefore, a given species can be more or less drought tolerant depending on the trait under consideration.
the functional traits that determine drought tolerance are not the same as those that are responsible for the response to drought.
the drought tolerance of individuals of a given taxon is not always predictable by the functional traits of the species.
